candidate_sentences.text: Funding was strengthened through the first €250 million covered-bond issuance under a €750 million programme, providing longer-term financing and allowing the bank to reduce more expensive term and foreign deposits.

An agreement with the European Investment Bank Group is expected to provide capital relief and enable up to €249 million of new business lending, although it was not yet effective and had no impact on 2025 results.

verified_key_information_units.information: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio stands at 14.15%, Tier 1 capital ratio at 16.11%, and total capital ratio at 18.54%, meeting all regulatory requirements; designated as systemically important with an additional buffer requirement.

candidate_sentences.text: Capital ratios declined as risk-weighted assets grew, with the CET1 ratio at 14.15% and total capital ratio at 18.54%, but all regulatory requirements were met.

verified_key_information_units.information: Implemented LEED Platinum-certified headquarters, paperless operations, IT equipment recycling, and financing of solar/wind parks (81.3 MW); secured European Investment Bank funding for gender equality and climate action projects.

Launched virtual card services, expanded branch network (including Valga and Viljandi), introduced a cashback program, and rolled out new loan products for small businesses and specific professions (e.g., Teacher's Home Loan, Home Defender Home Loan).
Distributed €7.2 million in dividends (25% of 2024 pre-tax profit) at €0.07 per share; proposed €6.7 million in dividends (0.065€ per share) from 2025 profit, taxed at 22/78 rate.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Dividend policy (page 24) and Proposal for profit allocation (page 134)

candidate_sentences.text: The bank paid €7.2 million in dividends for 2024 and proposed a 2025 dividend of €0.065 per share, totaling €6.7 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: In February 2026, drew a €5 million subordinated loan from the European Energy Efficiency Fund (EEEF), classified as Tier 2 capital, to finance energy efficiency and renewable energy projects.
On 21 January 2026, Alvar Pihlapuu was appointed as a new Member of the Management Board.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (profitability metrics), K2 (loan portfolio growth), K3 (deposit growth), K4 (customer base expansion), K6 (funding initiatives), K7 (capital ratios), and K10 (dividend distribution). However, it omits the strategic targets outlined in K5, sustainability initiatives described in K8, product/service expansions in K9, the 2026 EEEF loan in K11, and the management board appointment in K12. While several HIGH-importance items are missing, the summary captures most of the key financial and operational developments, resulting in a Generally yes rating.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support each other without contradiction. The narrative flows from overall performance to specific income components, expenses, balance sheet items, and capital adequacy. Explanations (e.g., falling interest rates impacting profitability) consistently explain observed changes. There is no self-contradiction, logical gap, organizational flaw, or unnecessary repetition. All relationships between figures (e.g., income components contributing to net profit decline) are logically presented without implying arithmetic contradictions. The summary forms a clear, cohesive narrative of Coop Pank's 2025 financial performance.
